prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1085; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Insured reports a left-turn collision at an intersection. Insured states they were turning left on a green arrow when the other vehicle proceeded straight through from the opposing lane. Scene photos requested. Liability appears disputed at this stage.

Entry 2: Claimant has retained counsel. Attorney letter of representation received. All further contact to be routed through counsel. Claimant reports pain in the left knee following the impact and has been seen at urgent care. Medical authorization requested through counsel.

Entry 3: Reviewed police report. Officer notes both drivers gave conflicting accounts of the signal phase. Witness statement obtained from a pedestrian at the corner, who states the oncoming vehicle entered the intersection after the signal changed. Liability position under review.

Entry 4: Counsel's office requested a copy of the vehicle damage estimate and the insured's policy declarations page. Documents sent. Claimant's treating physician notes a knee strain with possible meniscus involvement. MRI ordered per records received. Reserve reviewed and adjusted upward for bodily injury exposure.

Entry 5: Spoke with defense liaison regarding the claim status. Recommend holding offer pending MRI results and final medical records. Diary set for follow-up with counsel. Liability remains at roughly even split pending review of the signal timing data and the witness interview.
